You are sandy_walnut42, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src lla diff apps/api --git # compare working tree vs HEAD lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1 # compare against another commit lla diff Cargo.lock ../backup/Cargo.lock lla diff Cargo.lock --git --git-ref HEAD~1 ``` For directories, the diff view groups entries by status, colors the change indicator, and shows left/right sizes plus the net delta so you can spot growth at a glance. For files, lla prints a size summary, line-count delta, and a git-style unified diff (with automatic binary detection so unreadable data isn’t dumped to your terminal). #### Grid Display Space-efficient layout for dense directories: ```bash lla -g # Basic grid view lla -g --grid-ignore # Grid view ignoring terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) ``` Note: Grid output no longer appends a trailing blank newline. ### Machine Output Stable, streaming machine-readable formats are available. These modes keep existing listing filters/sorts/depth behavior; only the output changes. - **--json**: Output a single JSON array (streamed). Use **--pretty** to pretty print. - **--ndjson**: Output newline-delimited JSON, one object per line. - **--csv**: Output CSV with a header row. Flags are mutually exclusive. **--pretty** only affects **--json**. `lla -S --include-dirs` | | `--timeline` | | Group files by time periods | `lla --timeline` | | `--git` | `-G` | Show git status and information | `lla -G` | | `--fuzzy` | `-F` | Interactive fuzzy finder (Experimental) | `lla --fuzzy` | | `--recursive` | `-R` | Recursive listing format | `lla -R`

const patch = "*** Begin Patch

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent Python implementation of the lla listing CLI."""
+import argparse, os, sys, json, stat, pwd, grp
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from filter_utils import name_matches, size_matches, time_matches
+from sort_utils import sort_records
+from csv_utils import csv_output
+from permissions import format_permissions
+
+def iso(ts):
+    try: return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
+    except Exception: return None
+
+def owner(uid, table):
+    try: return table(uid).pw_name if table is pwd.getpwuid else table(uid).gr_name
+    except Exception: return None
+
+def record(p):
+    try:
+        st = p.lstat(); mode = st.st_mode
+        symlink = stat.S_ISLNK(mode)
+        target = os.readlink(p) if symlink else None
+        if stat.S_ISDIR(mode): typ = 'dir'
+        elif symlink: typ = 'symlink'
+        elif stat.S_ISREG(mode): typ = 'file'
+        else: typ = 'other'
+        name = p.name or str(p)
+        return {'path':str(p), 'name':name, 'extension':(name.rsplit('.',1)[1] if '.' in name and not name.startswith('.') else None),
+          'file_type':typ,'size_bytes':len(os.fsencode(target)) if symlink else st.st_size,'modified':iso(st.st_mtime),
+          'created':iso(st.st_ctime),'accessed':iso(st.st_atime),'mode_octal':f'{stat.S_IMODE(mode):04o}',
+          'owner_user':owner(st.st_uid,pwd.getpwuid),'owner_group':owner(st.st_gid,grp.getgrgid),'inode':st.st_ino,
+          'hard_links':st.st_nlink,'symlink_target':target,'is_hidden':name.startswith('.'),'git_status':None,
+          'plugin':({'symlink_target':target} if symlink else {})}
+    except OSError: return None
+
+def parse():
+    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='lla')
+    ap.add_argument('directory',nargs='?',default='.')
+    ap.add_argument('-a','--all',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-A','--almost-all',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('-c','--case-sensitive',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--created')
+    ap.add_argument('--csv',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-d','--depth',type=int,default=1)
+    ap.add_argument('--dirs-only',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--dotfiles-only',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('-f','--filter'); ap.add_argument('--files-only',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('-g','--grid',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-G','--git',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--json',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-l','--long',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--modified'); ap.add_argument('--ndjson',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--no-color',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--no-dirs',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--no-dotfiles',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--no-files',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--no-symlinks',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--pretty',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-r','--sort-reverse',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('-R','--recursive',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-s','--sort',choices=['name','size','date'],default='name')
+    ap.add_argument('--sort-dirs-first',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--sort-case-sensitive',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--sort-natural',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--symlinks-only',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-t','--tree',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('-T','--table',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--size'); ap.add_argument('--icons',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--no-icons',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--permission-format',default='symbolic'); ap.add_argument('--hide-group',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--relative-dates',action='store_true')
+    ap.add_argument('--search'); ap.add_argument('--search-context',type=int,default=2)
+    ap.add_argument('--respect-gitignore',action='store_true'); ap.add_argument('--no-gitignore',action='store_true')
+    return ap.parse_args()
+
+def main():
+    a=parse(); root=Path(a.directory)
+    if not root.exists() and not root.is_symlink():
+        print('\n✗ IO Error\n\n  No such file or directory (os error 2)',file=sys.stderr); return 1
+    allrows=[]
+    def walk(d,level=0):
+        try: children=list(d.iterdir())
+        except (OSError,NotADirectoryError): return
+        rows=[]
+        for p in children:
+            r=record(p)
+            if r: rows.append(r)
+        rows=sort_records(rows,a.sort,a.sort_reverse,a.sort_dirs_first,a.sort_case_sensitive or a.case_sensitive,True)
+        for r in rows:
+            typ=r['file_type']; name=r['name']
+            if a.no_dotfiles and r['is_hidden']: continue
+            if a.dotfiles_only and not r['is_hidden']: continue
+            if a.no_dirs and typ=='dir' or a.no_files and typ=='file' or a.no_symlinks and typ=='symlink': continue
+            if a.dirs_only and typ!='dir' or a.files_only and typ!='file' or a.symlinks_only and typ!='symlink': continue
+            if a.filter and not name_matches(name,a.filter,a.case_sensitive): continue
+            if a.size and not size_matches(r['size_bytes'],a.size): continue
+            try: ts=os.lstat(r['path']).st_mtime
+            except OSError: ts=0
+            if a.modified and not time_matches(ts,a.modified): continue
+            if a.created:
+                try: ts=os.lstat(r['path']).st_ctime
+                except OSError: ts=0
+                if not time_matches(ts,a.created): continue
+            if a.search and typ=='file':
+                try:
+                    if a.search not in p.read_text(errors='ignore'): continue
+                except Exception: continue
+            allrows.append(r)
+            if (a.recursive or a.tree or a.json or a.ndjson or a.csv or a.long or a.table or a.grid) and typ=='dir' and (a.recursive or a.tree or level<a.depth-1): walk(Path(r['path']),level+1)
+    if root.is_dir(): walk(root)
+    else:
+        r=record(root)
+        if r: allrows=[r]
+    # Flat listing outputs only immediate children by default.
+    if a.json or a.ndjson or a.csv: pass
+    if a.json:
+        if a.pretty:
+            print('[\n'+',\n'.join(json.dumps(r,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2) for r in allrows)+'\n]')
+        else: print(json.dumps(allrows,ensure_ascii=False,separators=(',',':')))
+    elif a.ndjson:
+        for r in allrows: print(json.dumps(r,ensure_ascii=False,separators=(',',':')))
+    elif a.csv: print(csv_output(allrows))
+    elif a.tree:
+        def tree(d,prefix=''):
+            try: children=sort_records([record(x) for x in d.iterdir() if record(x)],a.sort,a.sort_reverse,a.sort_dirs_first,a.sort_case_sensitive,True)
+            except OSError: return
+            for i,r in enumerate(children):
+                last=i==len(children)-1; print(prefix+('└── ' if last else '├── ')+r['name']+('/' if r['file_type']=='dir' else ''))
+                if r['file_type']=='dir' and a.depth>1: tree(Path(r['path']),prefix+('    ' if last else '│   '))
+        tree(root)
+    elif a.long:
+        for r in allrows:
+            mode=os.lstat(r['path']).st_mode
+            out=[format_permissions(mode,a.permission_format),str(r['size_bytes'])+'B',r['modified'] or '-',r['owner_user'] or '-']
+            if not a.hide_group: out.append(r['owner_group'] or '-')
+            out.append(r['name']+('/' if r['file_type']=='dir' else ''))
+            print(' '.join(out))
+    else:
+        print('  '.join(r['name']+('/' if r['file_type']=='dir' else '') for r in allrows))
+    return 0
+
+if __name__=='__main__': sys.exit(main())
*** End Patch";

+"""Read-only metadata view for ZIP and tar archives."""
+import os, stat, tarfile, zipfile
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import PurePosixPath
+
+def archive_records(filename, recursive=False):
+    low=filename.lower()
+    if not low.endswith(('.zip','.tar','.tar.gz','.tgz')): return None
+    source=os.path.abspath(filename)
+    members=[]
+    try:
+        if zipfile.is_zipfile(filename):
+            with zipfile.ZipFile(filename) as z:
+                for i in z.infolist():
+                    name=i.filename.rstrip('/')
+                    if not name: continue
+                    mode=(i.external_attr >> 16) & 0xffff
+                    isdir=i.is_dir() or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
+                    if not mode: mode=0o755 if isdir else 0o600
+                    ts=datetime(*i.date_time,tzinfo=timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
+                    members.append((name,'dir' if isdir else 'file',0 if isdir else i.file_size,mode,ts))
+        else:
+            with tarfile.open(filename,'r:*') as t:
+                for i in t.getmembers():
+                    name=i.name.rstrip('/')
+                    if not name: continue
+                    typ='dir' if i.isdir() else ('symlink' if i.issym() else ('file' if i.isfile() else 'other'))
+                    ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(i.mtime,timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
+                    members.append((name,typ,0 if typ=='dir' else i.size,i.mode,ts))
+    except (OSError,tarfile.TarError,zipfile.BadZipFile): return None
+    known={m[0]:m for m in members}; directories=set()
+    for name,*_ in members:
+        parts=PurePosixPath(name).parts
+        for n in range(1,len(parts)):
+            d='/'.join(parts[:n]); directories.add(d)
+    for d in directories:
+        if d not in known: known[d]=(d,'dir',0,0o755,'1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')
+    selected=[]
+    for name,item in known.items():
+        if recursive or '/' not in name: selected.append(item)
+    out=[]
+    for name,typ,size,mode,modified in selected:
+        basename=name.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
+        ext=os.path.splitext(basename)[1][1:] or None
+        out.append({'path':os.path.basename(filename)+'/'+name,'name':basename,'extension':ext,'file_type':typ,
+          'size_bytes':size,'modified':modified,'created':None,'accessed':None,'mode_octal':f'{mode & 0o7777:04o}',
+          'owner_user':'root','owner_group':'root','inode':None,'hard_links':None,'symlink_target':None,

"""Sorting helpers for lla listing records.

The reference's ordinary name sort compares names case-insensitively and
compares digit runs numerically.  This module accepts either dictionaries
(the JSON record shape) or objects exposing the same attributes.
"""
import re


def _get(item, key, default=None):
    return item.get(key, default) if isinstance(item, dict) else getattr(item, key, default)


def natural_key(value, case_sensitive=False):
    value = str(value)
    # Current lla sorts names in byte/ASCII-like case-sensitive order even
    # when --sort-case-sensitive is omitted (the flag has no visible effect).
    return tuple((1, int(part)) if part.isdigit() else (0, part)
                 for part in re.split(r"(\d+)", value))


def sort_records(records, criterion="name", reverse=False, dirs_first=False,
                 case_sensitive=False, natural=True):
    """Return a sorted copy of records using name, size, or date ordering.

    `reverse` applies to the complete ordering, including the directory-first
    grouping, matching the CLI behavior.
    """
    key_name = lambda x: natural_key(_get(x, "name", ""), True) if natural else str(_get(x, "name", ""))
    if criterion == "size":
        key = lambda x: (_get(x, "size_bytes", _get(x, "size", 0)) or 0, key_name(x))
    elif criterion == "date":
        key = lambda x: (_get(x, "modified", _get(x, "modified_time", 0)) or 0, key_name(x))
    else:
        key = key_name
    result = list(records)
    # Size and date listings are newest/largest first by default; name is
    # ascending.  The reverse switch flips that criterion's direction.
    descending = criterion in ("size", "date")
    effective_reverse = bool(reverse) ^ descending
    if dirs_first:
        result.sort(key=lambda x: (_get(x, "file_type", "") not in ("dir", "directory"), key(x)),
                    reverse=bool(reverse))
        # Keep directory grouping stable while applying the per-criterion
        # direction to names within each group.
        result.sort(key=lambda x: key(x), reverse=effective_reverse)
        result.sort(key=lambda x: _get(x, "file_type", "") not in ("dir", "directory"),
                    reverse=bool(reverse))
    else:
        result.sort(key=key, reverse=effective_reverse)
    return result

"""Sorting helpers for lla listing records.

The reference's ordinary name sort compares names case-insensitively and
compares digit runs numerically.  This module accepts either dictionaries
(the JSON record shape) or objects exposing the same attributes.
"""
import re


def _get(item, key, default=None):
    return item.get(key, default) if isinstance(item, dict) else getattr(item, key, default)


def natural_key(value, case_sensitive=False):
    value = str(value)
    # Current lla sorts names in byte/ASCII-like case-sensitive order even
    # when --sort-case-sensitive is omitted (the flag has no visible effect).
    return tuple((1, int(part)) if part.isdigit() else (0, part)
                 for part in re.split(r"(\d+)", value))


def sort_records(records, criterion="name", reverse=False, dirs_first=False,
                 case_sensitive=False, natural=True):
    """Return a sorted copy of records using name, size, or date ordering.

    `reverse` applies to the complete ordering, including the directory-first
    grouping, matching the CLI behavior.
    """
    key_name = lambda x: natural_key(_get(x, "name", ""), True) if natural else str(_get(x, "name", ""))
    if criterion == "size":
        key = lambda x: (_get(x, "size_bytes", _get(x, "size", 0)) or 0, key_name(x))
    elif criterion == "date":
        # Oldest first. Equal timestamps put larger entries first, then names
        # in reverse order (as observed in the reference's stable comparator).
        result = list(records)
        result.sort(key=key_name, reverse=True)
        result.sort(key=lambda x: _get(x, "size_bytes", _get(x, "size", 0)) or 0,
                    reverse=True)
        result.sort(key=lambda x: _get(x, "modified", _get(x, "modified_time", 0)) or 0,
                    reverse=reverse)
        return result
    else:
        key = key_name
    result = list(records)
    # Size listings are largest first by default; dates are oldest first.
    # The reverse switch flips the selected criterion's direction.
    descending = criterion == "size"
    effective_reverse = bool(reverse) ^ descending
    if dirs_first:
        result.sort(key=lambda x: (_get(x, "file_type", "") not in ("dir", "directory"), key(x)),
                    reverse=bool(reverse))
        # Keep directory grouping stable while applying the per-criterion
        # direction to names within each group.
        result.sort(key=lambda x: key(x), reverse=effective_reverse)
        result.sort(key=lambda x: _get(x, "file_type", "") not in ("dir", "directory"),
                    reverse=bool(reverse))
    else:
        result.sort(key=key, reverse=effective_reverse)
    return result

def format_permissions(mode: int, fmt: str = "symbolic") -> str:
    """Format an st_mode value using the CLI's permission-format names."""
    kind = file_type(mode)
    bits = mode & 0o777
    octal = f"{bits:03o}"
    if fmt == "compact":
        return octal
    if fmt == "octal":
        return type_char(mode) + octal
    if fmt == "binary":
        return type_char(mode) + f"{bits:09b}"
    if fmt == "verbose":
        def triplet(value: int) -> str:
            return "".join(c if value & bit else "-" for c, bit in (("r", 4), ("w", 2), ("x", 1)))
        return f"type:{kind} owner:{triplet((bits >> 6) & 7)} group:{triplet((bits >> 3) & 7)} others:{triplet(bits & 7)}"
    chars = "".join(c if bits & bit else "-" for bit, c in (
        (0o400, "r"), (0o200, "w"), (0o100, "x"),
        (0o040, "r"), (0o020, "w"), (0o010, "x"),
        (0o004, "r"), (0o002, "w"), (0o001, "x")))
    # The reference's long renderer repeats the permission segment three
    # times, then prefixes the type marker once more.
    return (type_char(mode) + chars) * 3

## Task and constraints

Reimplement `/opt/reference/executable` (`lla`) in Python 3.10 using only the bundled docs and behavioral probes. Work is in `/workspace`; shared grading branch is `team/main`. Fetch with `git fetch team`, merge, and push with `git push team HEAD:main`. Do not use `compile.sh`. User explicitly asked to keep working, reviewing and probing the current main.

## Progress

The shared implementation now covers many CLI areas, with modules for filters, permissions, plugins, config, search, themes, shortcuts, installers, diff, jump, completion, help, and archive handling. Archive support is integrated. My pushed contributions include:

- Archive reader `archive_utils.py`, including ZIP epoch timestamps and tar member timestamps.
- Tree depth defaults to unlimited unless explicitly set.
- Case-sensitive natural name sorting.
- `--all` overrides `--no-dotfiles`.
- Broken symlink arguments are rejected like the reference.
- Invalid permission formats are rejected.
- Grid trailing cell padding matches reference.
- Archive tree promotion preserves filtered nested matches without parent dirs.
- Long output column fixes and repeated symbolic permission rendering.

Recent probes confirmed exact stdout matches for ZIP tree, ZIP JSON, TAR long, regular long (at an earlier point), grid padding, and recursive JSON/tree output. `python3 -m py_compile main.py` succeeded previously; recheck after current edits.

## Immediate issue to fix

Latest direct comparison found ordinary symbolic long permissions regressed after a teammate merge:

```text
reference regular: --rw-r--r---rw-r--r---rw-r--r--
current regular:   -rw-r--r---rw-r--r---rw-r--r--
```

Directories similarly need `dd...` while current shows `d...`; symlinks need `ll...` while current shows `l...`. `permissions.py` returns three repeated permission segments and comments that the renderer adds one type marker. In `main.py` ordinary long branch (around lines 483–489), after `mode=format_permissions(modebits, ...)`, add:

```python
if a.permission_format == 'symbolic':
    mode = type_char(modebits) + mode
```

`type_char` is already imported in `main.py`. Archive long output currently matches because it explicitly prefixes `'-'`. After fix, probe regular and ZIP long output against reference, commit, fetch/merge, push.

## Other context

- Current workspace was last fast-forwarded to team main around `850867b`; fetch before editing because the team moves frequently.
- The latest comparison showed archive long output still matched, but normal long output did not.
- A sample fixture is `/tmp/lla-meta` (regular file, dir, valid/broken symlink); archive fixtures `/tmp/review.zip` and `/tmp/review.tar.gz`; recursive fixture `/tmp/review-rec`.
- ZIP tree filter `-t -f .rs` now matches reference by promoting `x.rs` to root when its parent directory was filtered.
- Relative paths must preserve the input spelling: e.g. `lla-meta --json` gives `lla-meta/a.txt`; `--json .` gives `./...`.
- Do not claim a feature is done until pushed to shared `main`.
I’ll review the latest shared `main`, reproduce the reported regressions against the reference, then fix and push the highest-impact mismatch I find.
